source.title: The “plant neurobiology” revolution

passages.excerpt_preview: It notes that Bose made the conceptual extension from motile plants to ordinary plants, while modern plant signaling does not imply that plants have animal neurons or brains.

passages.locator: transition from radio-wave physics to plant physiology
passages.excerpt_preview: The review places Bose’s transition from radio-wave physics to plant physiology in the early twentieth century and treats his instrumentation and questions as historically important to plant electrophysiology.

passages.locator: Burdon-Sanderson’s demonstration of plant action potentials
passages.excerpt_preview: he review dates Burdon-Sanderson’s demonstration of plant action potentials in Dionaea to 1873 and calls Bose a prolific early twentieth-century investigator of plant electrical responses.
